paper.title: You Only Look at Screens: Multimodal Chain-of-Action Agents
paper.central_claim: Auto-GUI is a multimodal agent that interacts directly with the screen without environment parsing or application-specific APIs, and a chain-of-action technique (previous action history plus future action plan) helps it decide what action to execute; it achieves state-of-the-art on AITW with 90% action-type accuracy and 74% overall action success rate. Scope as measured: offline screen-wise action matching on the five AITW subsets with fine-tuned 60M-700M models.

evidence.support_explanation: Our arithmetic: overall 74.27 (unified) vs BC-history 73.1 is +1.17; Auto-GUI separate 74.07 is +0.97. Unified is below BC-history on Install (76.89 vs 77.5) and GoogleApps (71.37 vs 75.7). No run-to-run spread is reported, so a 1-point margin cannot be tested.

Our reading: Table 3 and appendix Table 9 give the same two numbers (73.78 and 68.81) to opposite components. Both tables agree that removing the whole chain costs 5.74 points but disagree about whether the input history or the output plan carries it; the text never reconciles this.

Our reading: the fine-tuned Llama 2 baseline uses 1% of the training data (E015) and a different click metric (E007), and ICL baselines are few-shot with no training, so Table 2 does not isolate parsed-HTML input from training regime. The only matched-regime comparison is BC-history, which also consumes OCR/icon detections.

Our reading of the notation: the screenshot feature is stated as H_screen with shape 1 x d_s (one vector per screenshot) and the cross-attention keys/values are that single vector; how fine spatial information for 58% click-region accuracy is carried is not explained, and the encoder input resolution is not stated.

Searched main text, Tables 1-10, Limitations and Appendices A-C for: online/live execution results or AndroidWorld, repeated runs/seeds/confidence intervals, an ablation removing the vision input (language-only with history), measurement of parsing error propagation, instruction-disjoint splits or contamination check, a Llama-2 baseline trained on the same data, image resolution / feature shape, and how the predicted plan is used at inference. None reported. Figures 3-5 are images.

signatures.name: Parse-free screenshot policy with unified text action
signatures.object: Observation and action interface of a mobile GUI policy (baselines: OCR/icon-detector HTML into an LLM; BC with detected UI annotations)
signatures.information: Screenshot only (frozen BLIP-2 feature), goal, action text history; no OCR or detector output at inference by default; privileged signal at training = gold actions from AITW.
signatures.operation: Fuse language encoder states (goal + history) with a projected image feature through single-head attention and gated fusion; T5-style decoder emits {Action Plan, Action Decision} as a string with action type, touch point, lift point, typed text.
signatures.output: Action string: dual-point gesture (click/scroll), type, go_back, go_home, enter, status_complete.
signatures.conditions: Fine-tuned on AITW; 60M-700M parameters; max input length 512.
signatures.selection_rule_data: None; supervised cross-entropy on gold actions.
signatures.later_use: Evaluated on held-out episodes of the same subsets.
signatures.claimed_effect: SOTA overall 74.27 vs BC-history 73.1; inference under one second; 10x faster than Llama 2.
signatures.failure_boundary: Click region and scroll direction accuracy; unified model trails BC-history on Install and GoogleApps; single benchmark.

signatures.name: Chain of action
signatures.object: History input and plan output of the policy
signatures.information: Up to 8 previous actions (type, touch, lift, text) as text; predicted up to 4 future action types before the current action; gold plan from the episode at training.
signatures.operation: Prepend action text history to the goal; make the decoder emit a future action-type plan then the action decision.
signatures.conditions: Windows chosen from the General subset analysis.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Window sizes chosen on the General subset (split unstated).
signatures.claimed_effect: Removing the chain costs 5.74 points (74.27 to 68.53).
signatures.failure_boundary: Table 3 vs Table 9 disagree on whether history or plan carries the effect.

signatures.name: Coordinate normalisation
signatures.operation: Keep four decimals for clicks; map every scroll to fixed directional coordinates (up/down/left/right).
signatures.failure_boundary: Loses scroll magnitude; effect measured once.

gap.author_gap: Parsing the screen with OCR/icon detectors gives long inputs, inference inefficiency and error propagation, and sandboxed approaches need application-specific APIs that third-party apps rarely expose.
gap.checked_gap: Efficiency part is evidenced (Table 5, Llama 2 hosted baseline). Error-propagation part is asserted but not measured; the authors own Table 10 shows parsed screen descriptions still add 2.7 points, which shows the parse channel carries information. API-inaccessibility is true for deployment but is not tested by an AITW offline benchmark.

claims.text: Auto-GUI achieves state-of-the-art on AITW: 74.27 overall, action-type accuracy about 90%.
claims.setting: AITW five subsets, offline screen-wise action matching, 80/10/10 episode-wise split; unified model uses 10% GoogleApps.
claims.baseline_control: BC-history 73.1 (copied), BC-single 68.7, PaLM-2-CoT 39.6, ChatGPT-CoT 7.72, GPT-4V 52.96 (copied), fine-tuned Llama 2 28.40 (own, 1% data).
claims.selection_vs_test: Chain length chosen from analysis on General; hyperparameter selection split not stated.
claims.result_denominator: Per-subset accuracy; episodes/steps counts of test sets not stated in the extracted text; single run.
claims.counterevidence: Margin over BC-history is +1.17 (unified) / +0.97 (separate); unified is lower on Install and GoogleApps (E029); no variance; instruction repeats across train and test.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On AITW offline matching, Auto-GUI is on par with or slightly above the strongest prior specialised baseline; SOTA by a small margin that cannot be tested for significance.

claims.text: Chain of action (history + future plan) contributes +5.74 points and coordinate normalisation +4.04.
claims.setting: Ablation on the unified model (Tables 3 and 9).
claims.counterevidence: Which half of the chain matters is contradicted between Table 3 and Table 9 (E039).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Removing the whole chain lowers the score by 5.74 in both tables; the allocation between history and plan is unresolved.

claims.text: Direct multimodal interaction beats LLMs on parsed HTML and removes parsing cost.
claims.baseline_control: ICL PaLM-2/ChatGPT (5-shot CoT), fine-tuned Llama 2 (1% data).
claims.result_denominator: Per-category table on General test set.
claims.counterevidence: Llama baseline trained on 1% data and a different click metric (E040); parsed descriptions still help Auto-GUI by 2.7 (E025).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Auto-GUI is far above the authors LLM baselines, but the cause (modality vs training regime) is not isolated.

claims.text: Inference is under one second and over 10x faster than Llama 2 with far less memory.
claims.result_denominator: Seconds per inference and peak GPU memory; hardware beyond training GPUs not described.
claims.counterevidence: Llama 2 is a 7B model choice by the authors; no smaller LLM baseline.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A 200M-700M seq2seq model is much cheaper than a hosted 7B LLM on the same task format.

claims.text: The approach generalises to new task domains (train on one AITW subset, test on others).
claims.selection_vs_test: Subsets share apps and instruction templates.

assessment.author_claim_preserved: state-of-the-art autonomous GUI agent that interacts directly with screens, 90% action-type accuracy, 74% overall action success rate
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the AITW benchmark under offline screen-wise action matching, a 200M-700M parameter seq2seq policy with a frozen BLIP-2 image feature, action-text history and a predicted action-type plan reaches 74.3 overall, about one point above the copied BC-history figure (with two subsets lower), runs in under a second per action, and is far above the authors LLM baselines. Whether parsing is harmful, which half of the chain matters, and online or cross-benchmark performance are not established.
unresolved: instruction overlap between train and test
effect of single pooled image feature on localisation
assessment.reproduction: No reproduction run; author reports only.

G.reason: A real deployment limitation (runtime parsing and API dependence) with a nearest-neighbour set (BC-history, ICL LLMs, GPT-4V). The claimed accuracy damage from parse errors is never measured and the paper own Table 10 shows parsed descriptions still help by 2.7 points, so the bottleneck is only partly substantiated.

M.reason: The architecture and the action serialisation are specified, and normalising coordinates is a reasoned fix for ambiguous pixel targets. The causal story for why a predicted action-type plan helps is thin, and with a single 1 x d_s image feature it is unexplained how localisation is achieved; the key assumptions are weakly argued.

X.reason: Training details (sizes, epochs, lr, batch, hours), action schema, normalisation rule, chain lengths and baselines are specified; missing input resolution, feature shape and how the predicted plan is used at inference, and boundary conditions are stated only briefly.

E.measurement.reason: Offline screen-wise matching with a 14% tolerance and bounding-box match, a different matching rule for LLM baselines, and a validity argument that cites prior work; no online or executed check at all.

E.causality.reason: Real ablations exist (chain, coordinate normalisation, features, sizes, with/without screen descriptions) but the history-vs-plan attribution is inconsistent across two tables, and the headline comparison to LLM baselines is confounded by training regime (1% data, ICL).

E.holdout.reason: Random episode-wise split means the same instructions and apps occur in train and test; the unified model trails BC-history on two subsets; chain length chosen on analysis of one subset; transfer across subsets shown only as an image.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs; a 1-point headline margin without variance; per-subset and per-category breakdowns (click, scroll, type) are given, which supplies some failure denominators.

E.cost.reason: Parameters, training hours, inference time and GPU memory are reported against a baseline; the baseline choice (7B LLM) and hardware for inference timing are not fully specified.

status_reason: Complete body and appendix read; five figures are images and unavailable as text. All eight items resolved.
readable_summary: System method (parse-free screenshot policy + chain of action), score 50.0, offline AITW, claim scoped. Real efficiency gain and some ablations; but SOTA margin is about 1 point from single runs, baselines are in different regimes (Llama 2 on 1% data), Table 3 and Table 9 swap the history/plan ablation labels, train and test share instructions, and no online result.
